title: I created an endless ARPG that live generates new loot and enemies with fresh code on the fly. Give it a try
author: ichishibe
selftext:
I had this idea because I was looking for new, exciting ways to utilise AI in videogames. I thought it'd be cool to have a "endless" dungeon; one that spawns in new loot with new special attacks,  and new enemies with new mechanics, all with no human intervention.

Try it here:  
[Writ Below, The Endless Dungeon](https://writbelow-a587947860de.herokuapp.com/)

Some cool things to note:

Each 'Relic' or above tier item has its own unique ai-generated model, that's displayed on the character. Each with its own unique special effect.

Floors are generated with new enemies and loot the first time any player enters them, so an endgame player can truly be exploring a new frontier.

Come along and try if you like!

comments.author: Ok-Investment4414
comments.body: :-/ u made a bad prototype , games need graphics , and the walk motion is weird buddy feels like a chess bishop.

comments.author: CreativeProblem7803
comments.body: You chose the right font (Diablo 2 font) for the game, but the rest is pretty rough and leaves a bad impression with me. No collision on props, ugly characters, no icons for the hotbar, very rough hp bar. Only the item UI/inventory looks good and finished. even though a bit too much text imho.

replies.author: ichishibe
replies.body:
Thanks for the feedback, I definitely didn't spend enough time thinking about the feel/graphics of the game. Unfortunately in some sense the characters need to be ugly, since all of the loot is generated as people play, otherwise it'd get very expensive for me using the API. I can imagine large companies being able to do this though! 

The HP bar and icons for the hotbar can definitely be fixed!

replies.author: hateborne
replies.body:
> Unfortunately in some sense the characters need to be ugly, since all of the loot is generated as people play, otherwise it'd get very expensive for me using the API.

You have it directly linked to an AI tool for an online game? You're asking to wake up to a multi hundred (or thousand) dollar AI bill with this arrangement.

replies.author: ichishibe
replies.body: It's only people who push the latest floor, the rest of the players will see the loot that has been generated by whoever has pushed the frontier

replies.author: hateborne
replies.body:
That's irrelevant. All it takes is someone finding an exploit or way to abuse the system before you get annihilated financially. 

Is the API being called remotely, as in game client hits a server, then server makes the API call to the AI tooling?

replies.author: ichishibe
replies.body:
Yep that's how it works, I don't have auto-renew set on my API though and it only has $11 in. I feel like this must be a pretty normal use-case for an API though -  surely their thinking is that people use it in consumer-facing interfaces.

Having said that, if you're more educated in this area then I'm all ears. I'd like to remain not financially annihilated.
